Description:
Invictus embodies the true hackathon spirit, bringing together teams of bright minds to innovate and tackle challenges head-on. It's an electrifying journey of rapid development, creative problem-solving, and collaborative energy, culminating in a showcase of groundbreaking solutions. Get ready for an intense and inspiring competition where ingenuity shines!

General Rules:
1. Individual participation is not allowed.
2. Team members must be from the same institution/college.
3. All submissions and presentations must be original; plagiarism will lead to disqualification.
4. Teams must adhere to the time limits and instructions given by organizers.
5. Participants are expected to maintain decorum, professionalism, and team spirit.
6. The judges’ decision is final and binding.
7. Organizers reserve the right to modify event structure or rules if necessary.

Event Structure (Rounds):
● Team Vibes:
  ○ You need 2 or 3 people per team. No lone wolves or big squads allowed!
  ○ Only 60 teams can sign up on the website, so get in quick!
● How it All Goes Down (Rounds!):
  ○ There's a pre-event 'Eliminatory Round' and then three main rounds.
● Eliminatory Round (The First Cut):
  ○ Two days before the big event, all 60 registered teams get the competition theme.
  ○ You then have to submit a one-page document explaining your problem statement and how you'd solve it.
  ○ Only 30 teams make it through this round. Those 30 teams then start building their prototypes for the main event!
● Round 1: Prototype Check-in & Advice:
  ○ Starts right at 8:30 AM – don't be late!
  ○ Show off the prototype you've already built.
  ○ This is chill – examiners will give you feedback and tips on how to make your prototype even better. Think of it as a helpful brainstorming session!
  ○ You'll need to use their suggestions for the next stage.
● Round 2: The First Real Challenge (Elimination Time):
  ○ You get 4 hours of development time before this round, so use it wisely!
  ○ This round happens from 12:30 PM to 2:00 PM.
  ○ Teams are scored out of 50 points.
  ○ Only the top 5 to 7 teams get to move on to the final round.
● Round 3: The Grand Finale!
  ○ After lunch, from 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM.
  ○ The remaining teams show off their improved solutions.
  ○ Another score out of 50 points.
  ○ The winners are decided by adding up your scores from Round 2 and Round 3.

Good luck!

Round Timings:
Round 1 - 4hrs
Round 2 - 1.5hrs
Round 3 Final - 1hr

To conceptualize, design, and test an aerodynamic model either through CAD design or by building a physical prototype. Both categories will be judged on equal criteria to ensure fair evaluation of innovation and engineering precision.

Participation Guidelines:
1. The event is open to all engineering students across all branches.
2. Team size: A maximum of 3 participants.
3. Each team can submit either a CAD model or a physical prototype (or both).
4. The design should focus on aerodynamics, efficiency, and structural feasibility.
5. Models should represent innovation, simplicity, and real-world applicability.
6. Participants should be ready to explain their design process, objectives, and results.
7. CAD models must be designed using professional CAD software (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, CATIA, etc.).
8. Physical prototypes should be self-built and safe for display and testing.

General Rules:
1. Teams must adhere to safety and ethical guidelines during model preparation.
2. Plagiarism or pre-built model submissions will lead to disqualification.
3. The judges’ decision will be final and binding.
4. All teams must present their work within the allotted time.
5. Certificates will be awarded to winners and participants.

At Secret Signals, participants step into a world of hidden meanings. Each stage will challenge your reasoning, observation, and teamwork through dynamic tasks and analytical challenges. The competition intensifies with every round, leaving only the most perceptive minds to decode the final mystery.

Team Details:
Team Size: 4 members
Maximum Registrations: 80 teams

General Rules:
1. Each team must consist of exactly four members - no more, no less.
2. Each team must carry at least one laptop for the event activities.
3. All participants are expected to maintain fair play and sportsmanship.
4. The use of unfair means or external assistance will result in disqualification.
5. Instructions provided by the event coordinators must be strictly followed.

Rounds Overview:
Round 1 - The Signal Test: Teams will tackle a series of reasoning and analytical tasks that assess mental agility and quick decision-making.
Round 2 - The Mystery Challenge: The next phase introduces an element of surprise, revealed only during the event.
Round 3 - The Final Signal: The first team to decipher all signals and reach the ultimate solution will emerge as the winner.

Round Timings:
Round 1 - 90 minutes
Round 2 - 3 hours
Round 3 - 3 hours

The Architectural Quiz is an exciting team-based competition, where each team consists of two members. Participants will engage in a challenging series of questions covering a wide range of topics related to architecture — including architectural styles, Indian and international architecture, building materials, construction technology, and related art forms.

Test your knowledge, teamwork, and passion for architecture in this intellectually stimulating event.

General Rules:
1. Only team entries are allowed; each team must have exactly 2 members.
2. The quiz-master’s decisions are final and cannot be challenged.
3. Use of mobile phones or electronic devices is prohibited in the final round.
4. Questions will cover themes such as Architectural Styles, Indian and International Architecture, Books, Materials, Technology, and Arts related to architecture.
5. Question formats include multiple choice, true/false, and short answer.
6. Audience/supporters cannot give hints.
7. No replacement of participants after registration.

Rounds Structure:
Preliminary Round:
• Format: 10-minute timed session
• Marks: 1 mark per question
• Selection: Top 8 teams qualify for elimination round

Elimination Round:
• Format: Objective multiple choice questions
• Time: 10 minutes
• Marks: 1 mark per question
• Selection: Top 4 teams qualify for final round

Final Round:
• Structure: General, Visual, Rapid Fire and Stage Rounds
• Scoring: 10 marks per correct answer
• Response Time: 30 seconds per question
• Team discussion allowed
• Tie breaker: 5 additional questions if scores are tied

STEM is a poster presentation event that provides a platform for B.Sc. students to showcase innovative scientific ideas and concepts under the theme “Shaping Tomorrow.” Participants present creative solutions and research-based posters in areas such as sustainable technologies, energy innovations, and emerging scientific advancements. The event aims to inspire young minds to think critically and contribute to building a better scientific future.

Rules:
1. Eligibility: The event is open exclusively to B.Sc. students from all science streams and colleges.
2. Team Composition: Each team must consist of 2 members. Inter-departmental teams are not allowed.
3. Registration: Teams must register before the deadline announced by the coordinators. Spot entries are not permitted.
4. Reporting: All participants must report 15 minutes prior to the event start time.
5. Discipline: Participants must maintain decorum throughout the event.
6. Event Guidelines: Participants must present an innovative idea, working model, or scientific concept related to the theme “Shaping Tomorrow.” The model or presentation must focus on one of the following areas: Water purification using natural adsorbents, Carbon capture and storage technologies, Microbial fuel cells – Energy from bacteria, Quantum computing – The next tech revolution. Time limit for presentation: 4 minutes for presentation + 2 minutes conclusion followed by short Q&A. Posters must be prepared by the participants themselves.
7. Judging Criteria: Creativity and Originality, Scientific Concept and Understanding, Relevance to Theme (“Shaping Tomorrow”), Presentation and Communication.

Round Timings:
Round 1 - 20 mins (4 hours) - single round event

Event Description:
Participants will design and fabricate a welded structure using the provided materials and tools within a limited timeframe. Using metal stocks such as rods, flats, angles, or sheets, teams will employ arc welding to create innovative and stable designs. Each structure will be evaluated on strength, design efficiency, and aesthetics, showcasing both technical skill and creative engineering.

Guidelines:
- Event Objective: Participants must design and fabricate a welded structure using given materials and tools within the specified time. The structure should demonstrate strength, stability, and creativity.
- Event Description: Teams will be provided with metal stock materials (rods, flats, angles, or sheets) and will use arc welding to build a structure that meets a given problem statement. The structure will be tested for strength, design efficiency, and aesthetics.

Rules:
1. Team Composition: Each team must consist of 2–4 members. All participants must be students from the same institution. Each team must have at least one member trained in basic welding operations.
2. Materials and Tools: Provided by organizers (raw material and safety equipment like safety goggles). Participants can bring extra safety equipment if desired.
3. Safety Rules: Safety gear is mandatory. Unsafe handling of tools or ignoring instructions will lead to disqualification. Maintain safe distance and avoid flammable materials near welding areas. Boiler suits are mandatory.
4. Disqualification Criteria: Use of pre-fabricated parts, unsafe acts, tampering, or exceeding time limits will result in disqualification.
5. Event Rounds:
   - Round 1 – Design & Planning: Teams sketch their concept and submit a design with dimensions. Judges evaluate feasibility, clarity, and material estimation. Fabrication: Teams fabricate the structure according to their approved design following safety rules. Time penalties apply for exceeding limits.
   - Round 2 – Testing & Evaluation: The final structure undergoes load or functionality testing for strength, stiffness, and finish.

Round Timings:
Round 1 - 120 minutes
Round 2 - 30 minutes

At ImagiX, teams set out on a creative adventure where technology meets storytelling. They solve fun clues and use AI tools to create unique stories. With every round, the challenge gets tougher, pushing teams to show their imagination, logic, and creativity in an AI-powered world.

General Rules:
1. Each team must have exactly two members.
2. Team members must be from the same college.
3. Only one laptop is allowed per team.
4. All work should be original and created using the provided AI tools.
5. Plagiarism or use of external materials is strictly prohibited.
6. Any kind of misconduct or unfair practice will lead to disqualification.
7. The event coordinators’ decisions will be final and binding.
8. Detailed instructions for each round will be given before that round begins.

Rounds Overview:
Round 1 – BrainSpark: Run your brain’s algorithm through brain teasers, riddles, aptitude, and logic tests. Score high to qualify for the next phase of imagination.
Round 2 – GenreQuest: Dive into a puzzle adventure filled with hints about characters, plots, and genres. Decode the mystery to reveal the genre needed for the upcoming round.
Round 3 – Tale Tailors: Phase 1: AI Tales – Use the genre you discovered to create a short story. You can use AI tools to brainstorm ideas, build characters, and shape your plot. Phase 2: The Final Revelation – A surprise twist awaits! Teams will face a new creative challenge designed to test both their storytelling and AI skills.

Round Timings:
Round 1 - 60 minutes
Round 2 - 60 minutes
Round 3 - 120 minutes

Urban Pulse is an engaging and competitive IoT-based pitching event designed to test participant’s knowledge, creativity, and problem-solving skills in the field of the Internet of Things (IoT). The event aims to encourage innovative thinking and the development of smart solutions that can make urban living more efficient and sustainable.

Event Rounds:
Round 1 - Quiz: A general IoT-based quiz will be conducted, after which the top 10 teams will be shortlisted for Round 2.
Round 2 - Idea Pitching:
Themes: Urban Disaster Management, Urban Agriculture and Resource Optimization, Smart Transport and Mobility.
Rules: Both team members must be present for the pitching round. A PowerPoint presentation (maximum of 8 slides) must be submitted at least 30 minutes prior to the start of Round 2. Each team will be allotted 6 minutes for the presentation, followed by a 2-minute Q&A session. Exceeding the time limit will lead to a deduction in marks. Judging criteria include: Idea Feasibility, Presentation Skills, Innovation, and Creativity. Bonus points may be awarded for presentations that are not AI-generated. The judge’s decisions will be final and binding.

Put your engineering instincts to the test! Troubleshooting is all about identifying faults, fixing circuits, and restoring them to life. Spot the errors, make it work, and prove your technical edge under pressure!

Rules:
1. Each team should consist of 2 to 3 members.
2. Teams can include students from any semester and any branch.
3. Inter-branch participation is allowed and encouraged.
4. Teams must report to the event venue 15 minutes before the scheduled start.
5. All required tools and components will be provided at the venue.
6. Use of mobile phones or external help is strictly prohibited and will lead to disqualification.
7. Any damage to components due to negligence will lead to disqualification.
8. Participants must use only the provided materials and instruments.
9. The decisions of the coordinators and judges will be final and binding.

Round Details:
Round 1 – Basic Fault Identification: A circuit diagram will be provided on paper. Participants must identify missing components, mention what the circuit does, and suggest corrections if required. Includes general MCQs from basic Electrical, Electronics, and other engineering branches. Total Marks: 30. Duration: 45 minutes. Top 20 performing teams will qualify for Round 2.

Round 2 – Troubleshooting Challenge: A setup will be provided to each team, which may include circuits, hardware, or programming tasks. The setup may contain wrong connections, missing components, errors in code, or extra parts. Teams must identify and correct the faults to make the setup functional. All required tools and components will be provided at the venue. 20 setups will be provided. Each setup should be solved within 2 minutes. Teams completing the setup accurately in the given time will qualify for the next round.

Round 3 – Mystery Round: A surprise task will be given on the spot. It will test the team’s technical knowledge, speed, and accuracy. Quick thinking and teamwork will decide the winners.

Round Timings:
Round 1 - 60 minutes
Round 2 - 60 minutes
Round 3 - 60 minutes

Laser Maze – The Quad Core Challenge: A team-based laser and mirror coordination challenge designed to test communication, timing, and precision under evolving restrictions. Each round introduces new conditions that demand focus, teamwork, and strategy. The team that maintains the highest points and completes all rounds in the shortest time will be declared the winner.

Rounds Overview:
Round 1 – The Open Maze Challenge: All four team members participate. Communication is open. Maze layout is complex, requiring planning and precise mirror placement. Laser Rule: ON for max 3 seconds at a time to check alignment. Time Limit: 3 minutes; penalties for exceeding 3 minutes; disqualification after 4 minutes. Start Score: 300 points; Major Violation: –10 points; Minor Violation: –5 points. Teams with 170+ points qualify.

Round 2 – The Blind Bridge Challenge: All four members participate with restricted communication. Instructor is the only one allowed to speak. Mirror Handlers blindfolded. Laser Bearer faces one direction; target behind. Laser ON only after adjustments, max 3 seconds. Scoring same as Round 1.

Round 3 – The Aqua Maze Finale: Conducted in water-filled fish tank with obstacles and mirrors. Same communication restrictions as Round 2. Laser ON max 3 seconds after adjustments. Unsafe handling or mirror contact = –5 points. Time Limit max 4 minutes; disqualification beyond. Objective: Direct laser beam to target accurately.

Judging: Each round starts with 300 points. Penalties applied for violations and time excess. Teams must secure minimum 60% points per round to advance. Final winner determined by highest cumulative score and shortest completion time. All coordinator decisions are final and binding.

Round Timings:
Round 1 - 300 minutes (60 teams)
Round 2 - 150 minutes (30 teams)
Round 3 - 60 minutes (10 teams)

The Stick Structure event is an exciting, hands-on event where participants explore engineering, creativity, and teamwork by building structures using simple sticks and glue. Teams design and construct the most innovative, stable, and efficient bridges, testing skills in structural integrity and design principles. Challenges include weight-bearing tests and structural stability evaluations. The event fosters collaboration, problem-solving, and hands-on learning.

Rules:
- Each team should consist of 2 to 4 members.
- Materials (sticks and glue) are provided.
- Maximum of 250 sticks per model.
- Bridge span: minimum 24cm, maximum 30cm.
- Sticks can be cut or notched.
- Model loaded at center after 24 hours of drying.
- No external materials allowed; violation leads to disqualification.
- Design must be completed within the assigned time.
- Screening test based on number of teams; top 10 advance.

Judging Criteria:
- Creativity
- Accuracy
- Minimum weight
- Maximum load capacity / strength
- Stability
- Aesthetic view

Round Timings:
Day 1: Screening & Round 1 - 30 mins (Venue: AS 27), Round 2 - 2 hours 30 mins (Venue: BMT Lab)
Day 2: Testing of models - 2 hours (Venue: BMT Lab)

VisionRacer is a high-speed, hands-on robotics competition where participants work with computer vision and autonomous control. Each team receives an identical robotics starter kit (chassis, DC motors, motor driver, battery, ESP32-CAM). Teams build and program an autonomous robot to visually detect and follow a complex track from start to finish. The competition involves assembly, programming, calibration, and on-track performance testing, emphasizing real-time image processing and high-speed navigation.

Rounds:
- Round 1: Preliminary Selection Round to assess robotics, computer vision, and control knowledge.
- Round 2: On-Site Build & Testing; teams assemble, program, and calibrate their robot.
- Round 3: On-Track Competition; autonomous robots complete the official VisionRacer track. Performance determines final winners.

Rules & Guidelines:
- Teams: 4 members; interdisciplinary participation allowed.
- Only provided kit components may be used; no external sensors.
- Minor mechanical modifications allowed; software must operate fully autonomously.
- Two official trials per team; time penalties for touches.
- Safety rules strictly enforced; violations lead to disqualification.

Evaluation: Final Score = Total Time - Penalties
